fields.label: feeler tentacle
fields.description: Thin, blind, and slow — it rises out of a still pool to search the shore after any loud noise. Harmless on its own; it is the one you see most, and the first sign that something enormous is paying attention.

fields.label: snare tentacle
fields.description: Thick, fast, and gripping, its underside ridged with suckers. It reaches for whatever wades too close and drags it toward the water. The killer of the six, and the reason nothing drinks at these pools unbothered.

fields.label: lash tentacle
fields.description: Long and barbed. It never grips; it strikes at maximum reach and withdraws, punishing anyone who lingers at the margin rather than crossing it.

fields.label: porter tentacle
fields.description: More slender and delicate than its kin — a courier, not a hunter. It rises just long enough to set something down at the water's edge: whatever was stripped from the great thing's last meal. Shoot it and the pool goes quiet on you forever; it never brings anything again.

fields.label: sentinel tentacle
fields.description: Motionless, raised just above the water. It does nothing — it listens, and the thing below hears very well. While this one is up the whole crown's chorus above falls silent to watch it. That silence is the loudest warning the Fever Wood has.

fields.label: bloom tentacle
fields.description: Vast. It does not reach — it opens, a ring of teeth around a pit of a throat, and for one long moment the eye beneath the Fever Wood is exposed. This is the near-glimpse of the thing itself, and the only moment it can truly be hurt.

fields.label: murrelith plumage
fields.description: Flat, translucent ribbon-plumes sheared from a murrelith's tail rather than plucked — they keep their colour and translucency long after the bird has grown a new set. Fetches a real price at market, which is exactly the problem: a colony living off the crown's silence is one bad trade away from a smaller warning.

fields.label: the Fever Wood
fields.description: The place where trees finally won. Great solid trunks, much more than one tile wide, have rooted the backswamp still and solid, tamed the flowing waters into shallow surface pools with deep, deep mud beneath. Their arches and branches have grown into byways well above the dark still pools -- roads made of living wood. In the crown: a whole arboreal world. Below: the black mirrors, unrippled. Nothing goes in the water here. Everything remembers why.

fields.label: captivity memory
fields.description: This animal was once held in a prison tank and broke free. Whatever the encounter is meant to cost it in the wild — its willingness to ever trust a hand again — is not yet tuned; the fact of it is remembered here.

fields.label: bound in kurreth paste
fields.description: Wrapped tight in a drying paste the kurreth spit, legs folded under. It is alive and unhurt, and cannot move until someone cuts it free.

fields.label: staked as lure
fields.description: Chained down at a lure stake, wounded and unable to break free. Whatever finds it first is not going to check whether it agreed to this.

fields.label: sap-sealed
fields.description: Bothered, this animal has flooded and set its own shell in hardened sap. It must be cracked open before anything more can be done to it.

fields.label: swollen
fields.description: Bothered, this animal has inflated until it cannot be pulled from its perch. Bursting it now would yield a large one-time harvest — and end this animal as a renewable source for good.

fields.label: bough-soil
fields.description: A living bed of silt and scale-mat, thick along the boughways and heaped where the trunks crown out — the only ground in the Fever Wood's canopy where anything can put down roots.

fields.label: boughway
fields.description: A living lane grown across the crown — bark and root woven flat and firm well above the black pools below. Fast, safe, and never quite where the map says it was last season.

fields.label: black mirror pool
fields.description: Still, black water, deep and unrippled. Big animals wander in to drink and are sometimes simply gone. Nothing sane touches it, and nothing explains why.

fields.label: stilt platform
fields.description: A heavy timber platform raised on driven piles, built to carry real weight over ground the marsh itself refuses. Costlier than a plain bridge deck, and worth every log — this is the only way to build heavy structures at ground level in the Fever Wood.

fields.label: kurreth resin plug
fields.description: Chewed earth and hardened resin, packed into a tunnel by kurreth workers in moments. It will crumble on its own in a few hours; anything in a hurry has to break it.

fields.label: lure stake
fields.description: A stout post driven into the ground, chain coiled at its base. Whatever gets tied here is meant to be found — by whatever is hunting nearby.

fields.label: sekkulaath prison tank
fields.description: A sealed, waterlogged cell, not a pen. Whatever is inside it did not agree to be there and is strong enough that it never has to — the tank holds because it is built to, not because the occupant tolerates it. Fed, it will produce; neglected or breached, it will not stay.

fields.label: fever trunk core
fields.description: The living heart of a giant trunk — the one cell of it that never goes still, and never mines out. Everything the tree does starts here, at a pace this whole biome shares.

fields.label: fever trunk heartwood
fields.description: The outer mass of a giant trunk, grown dense and still over the still water below — packed tight enough to dig into like stone. Cut a chamber into it and it heals, slower than the Greentide's own boles ever did; this biome does everything slowly.

fields.label: craft radioactive suppressant charge
fields.description: Machine raw Uranium down into a sealed charge that goes unstable fast once exposed — dump one into a Fever Wood pool to drive whatever lives beneath it down for days.

fields.label: murrelith plumage
fields.description: Flat, translucent ribbon-plumes sheared from a murrelith's tail rather than plucked — they keep their colour and translucency long after the bird has grown a new set. Fetches a real price at market, which is exactly the problem: a colony living off the crown's silence is one bad trade away from a smaller warning.

fields.label: thavrik egg (unfert.)
fields.description: An unfertilized thavrik egg, taken from a guarded nest high in the crown. Edible raw, much better cooked.

fields.label: thavrik egg (fert.)
fields.description: A fertilized thavrik egg. Left undisturbed, it hatches into a chick — taken instead, it is one less reason for the adults to still be circling.

fields.label: radioactive suppressant charge
fields.description: A sealed charge of processed Uranium, machined to go unstable fast and diffuse into whatever it is dumped into. Foul a Fever Wood pool with one and whatever lives beneath it goes quiet for days — the free-tier answer to a threat the campaign world only ever meets with rarer, more dangerous salvage.

fields.label: thornbug nectar
fields.description: Sweet, thick nectar wept by a calm thornbug — the dairy the arboreal cantons run on. A frightened herd dries up for days; every raid on the guild costs nectar before it costs blood.

fields.label: vaulm lacquer
fields.description: Amber-hard resin, cracked from a sealed vaulm's own shell. It sets glass-smooth and takes a fine finish — a real crafting material, and the reason anyone bothers a defended sap-sucker at all.

fields.label: drommath sap
fields.description: A thin trickle of sugar-sap, drawn off a swelling drommath without pushing it to burst. Renewable, for as long as the animal is left alone.

fields.label: burst drommath sap
fields.description: A gluttonous payout of sap, all at once, from a drommath burst rather than milked — this animal will never yield again. Worth far more than a season of the trickle it used to give.

fields.label: sekkulaath spleen chemicals
fields.description: A vial of thick, faintly luminous fluid drained from a captive sekkulaath's spleen. Brewed, it makes a narcotic tea that stains everything it touches purple.

fields.label: sekkulaath cream
fields.description: A pale, rich, faintly sweet secretion harvested from a fed captive sekkulaath, thick enough to fill pastry. It spoils quickly, same as any dairy off any animal.

fields.label: severed tentacle flesh
fields.description: A length of thick, rubbery flesh, still faintly warm, cut from a limb of whatever vast thing lives beneath the Fever Wood's pools. It grows back — eventually, on the animal, not in the pack. Traders who know the biome pay well for it; it renders into a rich meat and a strange, purple-tinged tea.

fields.label: mirror list
fields.description: A traders' ledger of which black pools have moved lately — ripples, silences, the mirrors that lied about where they were. Reading it marks the agitated pools on your map for a while. The list is a snapshot; the water keeps its own schedule.

fields.label: thulvane
fields.description: A colossal fused column of a tree, its base so broad it reads as several trunks grown together, rising past sight so its crown is simply a permanent green ceiling. Bark in wet vertical plates, black in the grooves, permanently damp. The biome's structural unit — the ceiling, the interlock that keeps anything from falling, and the body colonists mine rooms into.

fields.label: skethral
fields.description: Shorter and wider than a thulvane, and visibly reaching: its heavy limbs grow horizontally toward its neighbours and fuse where they meet, so two skethrals read as one arch. Bark smooth and pale at the joins, scarred where limbs have knitted. This is the tree that grows the boughway roads — the in-fiction reason the crown is interlocked at all.

fields.label: varnoth
fields.description: Rooted in a mirror pool itself, on a tripod of prop-roots clear of the surface, its trunk leaning out over the water. Its lower bark is stained and polished to a wet black by the pool. Nothing grows beneath it. Its timber is the best in the biome — and it stands inside the reach, so reward and hazard are the same object.

fields.label: plennith
fields.description: A dense low mat of overlapping grey-green scales lying directly along bark and bough, thickening into a spongy bed that visibly holds silt and rot. Reads as a surface, never as a plant. This is what makes the bough-soil — the crown's fertility is biological, not geological, and where plennith has run, other things can grow.

fields.label: ossagrel
fields.description: A thick segmented cane clamped along a bough, each joint swollen and split, weeping clear syrup that glazes and crusts below it. The whole plant looks over-full, and the bark under it is sugared and crawling. The host the crown's sap-suckers drink from, and the sugar line for stills and nectar-liquor.

fields.label: ossagrel sap
fields.description: Sugar-thick syrup wept from ossagrel canes. Distills into a rough liquor or ferments into nectar; the crown's own sap-suckers drink it straight from the plant.

fields.label: cistrel
fields.description: A tight rosette of stiff waxy leaves forming a cup at chest height, holding clear standing water you can see into — the only water on this map that is not black. Outer leaves rust-red, inner pale. The only safe water in the Fever Wood, where people and tame animals drink.

fields.label: maulith
fields.description: A crossbeam of stiff branches carrying a dense curtain of flat ribbon-leaves that falls to the walkway below, so the plant is a room with walls. Leaves olive above, silver-backed and always moving slightly. The concealment plant of the crown, and the boughway's privacy screen. Ribbon-leaf is cordage.

fields.label: verrow
fields.description: Few fronds, held high and thin, with heavy dull-skinned gourds hanging well below them on long stalks — the fruit is the visual mass, not the leaves. The crown's staple food, reachable from a boughway without climbing. Free calories that draw the crown's grazers, and then the things that wait for grazers.

fields.label: nubrith
fields.description: A low leathery dome on a squat stalk, glowing a steady warm amber downward onto the deck. The only natural light in the crown — deliberately warm, sitting beside the Wildsteam's steam-lamp gold rather than fighting it. A leaf that glows, not a mushroom.

fields.label: halquin
fields.description: Two broad blade-leaves lying flat and opposite against the trunk like a pressed specimen, dark and leathery, with a swollen joint between them that beads resin. The medicine — the resin is the biome's herbal medicine line, gathered by scraping, a safe patient crown-side income.

fields.label: ammeth
fields.description: One stiff flat fan of fused leaf held in a single plane from a short base, so it reads as a panel from one side and a line edge-on — the only plant here whose silhouette changes with facing. Waxy, rain-shedding, pale underneath. Roofing and decking; the cheapest building material in the biome, cut but never felled.

fields.label: claithe
fields.description: A flat rosette of blunt grey leaves over a broad pale root-plate that lifts clear of the mud, caked in grey clay it has bound out of the water. The potter's clay is harvested from its root-plate — a raw-terrain resource turned into a plant you can find, judge and farm at the water's edge.

fields.label: potter's clay
fields.description: Grey river clay, bound and lifted clear of the mud by a claithe's own root-plate. Workable straight from the plant.

fields.label: corvath
fields.description: A single thick dark-purple spike standing alone out of the mud, glossy and swollen, obviously better fed than anything around it. Always solitary — never more than a few at one pool. It grows only where the thing below has fed. A pool ringed with corvath is an occupied pool: the botanical tell that makes the pools readable. Worthless by design — its whole value is as information.

fields.label: sodderel
fields.description: A lopsided spar of a tree, half its limbs already dead and black with water, leaning permanently toward the pool. Living growth only on the high side. It looks like a wreck and is not one — this is the biome's ordinary construction wood, since the towers cannot be felled and varnoth is lethal to reach. It reads as naturally half-dead, not diseased.

fields.label: seepril
fields.description: A low dull barrel of a stem sitting in its own iridescent slick, the rainbow film spreading a cell or two around its base. Leafless above; just the barrel and the sheen. The seep-oils gather around it — perfume, lubricant, fuel. Its rainbow is the planet's honest register: just oil, just useful.

fields.label: seep oil
fields.description: Iridescent oil gathered from around a seepril's base. Perfume, lubricant or fuel, depending on who wants it.

fields.label: skimmel
fields.description: A continuous pale-green film lying perfectly flat over the mud, indistinguishable from firm ground until it is stepped on. Its only tell is that it is too even — no texture, no debris, and it never grows on ground that is actually solid. Disguises the sink-mud beneath it. ⚠️ Deliberately deceptive to the eye — do not "fix" this into looking safer or less like ground.

fields.label: wanlith
fields.description: Sparse colourless stalks a knee high, translucent and unbranched, standing in loose groups. Almost no biomass. Reads as absence — the visual proof that the floor is starved of light. The ground's baseline cover, deliberately worth almost nothing.

fields.label: tullick
fields.description: A tight low whorl of dull ribbed leaves with the ground visibly domed beneath it by the tuber below. The ground's one real reward — a bulk starch for the people working the causeway. Digging it churns the mud around it, an honest small cost.

fields.label: giant leaf
fields.description: An enormous, glossy leaf that grows low in the jungle understory, broad enough to shelter a grown man from the rain. Edible when young, and gathered as much for the shade as the food.

fields.label: giant leaf
fields.description: A giant and very impressive leaf.

fields.label: chellow
fields.description: Squat and round, with no feathers on its head at all — bare wrinkled skin and a translucent throat-fan it inflates to call, veined and lit faintly from behind. Easy to win over and easy to keep, a cultivated flock of chellow makes a private chorus outside the walls: as long as they are calling, the water below is quiet.

fields.label: murrelith
fields.description: Long-tailed, with flat translucent ribbons trailing where vaned quills should be — they hang and twist rather than spread. Those ribbons are worth real money, and that is exactly the temptation the crown sets against itself: sell the plumage and you have sold part of your own early warning.

fields.label: thavrik
fields.description: Heavy-bodied and short-winged, covered in coarse hair rather than feathers everywhere but the flight surfaces — a furred thing that flies. It nests high in the crown, eggs and nest material guarded by the adults: a reason to climb, if you can get past them.

fields.label: skellick
fields.description: Small and long-limbed, its plumes crumpled and unequal, sticking out at wrong angles as if damaged on purpose — the untidiest silhouette in the crown. It has learned to slip down and take small unattended things while nobody is looking, and it is very good at not being looked at.

fields.label: glomvar
fields.description:
A pale, eyeless, many-legged thing the size of a calf, its soft back slick with a film that smells exactly like a kurreth hive. The ants walk past it, over it, feed their young beside it, and never notice that their numbers keep shrinking. It eats one a day. When the hive is busy fighting something else, it eats more.

It has no interest in anything that is not a kurreth.

fields.label: kurreth
fields.description: A glossy red-black segmented ant the size of a large dog, oversized mandibles held forward as if perpetually mid-haul. Alone it is dangerous but not much of a threat; a whole hive of them is why nothing sensible digs where they have already dug.

fields.label: kurreth queen
fields.description: Vastly larger than any worker, sluggish outside her chamber, and never alone — a kurreth hive's queen is found only in its deepest room, worker escort pressed close around her.

fields.label: thornbug
fields.description: A great thorn-shaped insect clamped flush to the bark, secreting sweet, nourishing nectar in exchange for safety. The mechanic is the deal: it yields only while it feels safe, and a frightened herd dries up for days. Every raid on the crown costs nectar before it costs blood.

fields.label: vaulm
fields.description: A smooth swollen bead of amber on the bark, no limbs visible. Bothered, it floods its own shell and sets — armour, not flesh — and must be cracked open before anything more can be done to it. Killing and cracking it open yields a usable lacquer.

fields.label: ollareth
fields.description: Flat, wide, and ringed with open spiracles — bothered, it screams, and the whole crown answers. It yields nothing of its own; its value is that the biome fights for it, turning a theft raid into a fight the crown joins on your side.

fields.label: drommath
fields.description: A taut grey sac, visibly inflating. Handled, it swells rather than yield, until it cannot be pulled from its perch. Left calm, it can be milked for a small trickle of sap; burst instead, it pays out once, large — and never again.

fields.label: sekkulaath
fields.description: A small, dark, tentacled thing, kept in tanks because nothing else keeps it. It is not the elder being beneath the Fever Wood's pools — not yet — but it is unmistakably kin to it, and everyone who has heard it hum up close swears they will never mistake the sound again.

fields.label: captivity memory
fields.description: This animal was once held in a prison tank and broke free. Whatever the encounter is meant to cost it in the wild — its willingness to ever trust a hand again — is not yet tuned; the fact of it is remembered here.

designators.label: Cancel
designators.description: Cancel designated building, mining, hauling, harvesting, and all other designations.

designators.label: Deconstruct
designators.description: Deconstruct this and reclaim part of its resources.

designators.label: Mine
designators.description: Designate areas of rock to be mined out.

designators.label: Chop wood
designators.description: Marks trees to be chopped down for wood.

designators.label: Cut plants
designators.description: Marks plants to be cut and destroyed. The plant will be completely removed, and any food or resource yield will be harvested.

designators.label: Harvest
designators.description: Marks plants to be harvested for their food or other products.

designators.label: Hunt
designators.description:
Mark animals to be hunted by your hunters.

Only hunters with suitable ranged weapons will hunt.

designators.label: Slaughter
designators.description: Slaughter a tame animal.

designators.label: Tame
designators.description: Tame a wild animal.

designators.label: Haul things
designators.description: Mark rock chunks and other items to be hauled to dumping areas. Not needed for things like food or corpses, which are always haulable.

designators.label: Allow
designators.description: Mark items as not forbidden. Colonists will be able to interact with the designated items.

designators.label: Forbid
designators.description: Mark items as forbidden. Colonists will not be able to interact with the designated items.

designators.label: Claim
designators.description: Claim neutral structures for the colony, including ancient ruins and abandoned siege bases. Claimed structures can be repaired and maintained by your colonists.

designators.label: Smooth surface
designators.description: Designate rough stone terrain and walls to be smoothed.

designators.label: Paint building...
designators.description: Designate walls and buildings to be painted using dye from tinctoria plants, which you can grow. Only certain buildings can be painted.

designators.label: Paint floor...
designators.description: Designate floors to be painted using dye from tinctoria plants, which you can grow. Only certain floors can be painted.

designators.label: Remove paint
designators.description: Remove paint from walls, buildings, and floors.

designators.label: Plan
designators.description:
Place planning designations. These don't do anything except help you plan future expansions.

Right-click to hide or unhide all planning zones.

designators.label: Remove plans
designators.description: Remove planning designations.

designators.label: Export
designators.description: Export a building to xml

designators.label: Export from area
designators.description: Export a building to xml from area

designators.label: Dig canal
designators.description: Carve a channel one level deeper. Designating a channel that is already dug deepens it again — shallow, mid, deep, then SUPERDEEP. Liquid fills the deepest cells first and overflows into shallower ones. A channel dug into the strip along the map edge is a SINK: liquid reaching it leaves the map, which is how you empty a canal on purpose.

designators.label: Fill in canal
designators.description: Fill an excavated cell back in by one level. Liquid that no longer fits is pushed into the rest of the channel and back into the body it came from; only what finds no room anywhere is lost. Filling a cell all the way back to the surface restores the terrain that was there before it was dug.

designators.label: Apply deepfire
designators.description: Mark a wall, floor furniture, art piece, apparel or weapon for a colonist to coat in deepfire. Colour comes from however it is currently painted; deepfire adds the glow. Up to three coats, each brightening the light.

designators.label: Remove deepfire
designators.description: Strip all deepfire coats from a wall, floor furniture, art piece, apparel or weapon at once. No refund.

designators.label: Shovel sand
designators.description: Dig out loose sand for glass sand. The cell is shovelled down to what lies beneath (gravel), so a sand patch is a finite deposit. Done by miners.

designators.label: Stake as lure
designators.description: Flag a tamed animal or prisoner to be staked as living bait for the Fever Wood's raiders. It will be wounded down and chained in the open — there is no bloodless version of this.

designators.label: Foul pool with suppressant
designators.description: Mark a Fever Wood pool cell to be fouled with a radioactive suppressant charge (crafted from Uranium). A colonist will carry a charge there and dump it, driving whatever lives beneath the pool down for several days — no hostile encounters and no treasure trickle from that pool while it lasts.
